tooltips.silentStart: Start the program in background mode without displaying the panel
tooltips.connectOnLaunch: Right after launch the app raises the same connection method the button would. Off by default: nothing is written into the system until you ask for it.
tooltips.dnsOverride: macOS only: while the tunnel is up the system resolver is switched to a public one, so queries the system sends past the interface still go through the tunnel. Turn it off and part of them will go outside the tunnel.

sysproxy.coreGaveUp: The core stopped restarting, but the system proxy still points at it — nothing will go through it until the proxy is off or the core runs again.
sysproxy.coreNotRunning: The system proxy was not turned on: the core is not running.
sysproxy.writeFailed: The system did not accept the proxy settings.

tunMode.autoDisabled: The TUN adapter could not be created, so TUN is off. Try turning it on again; the details are in the application log
tunMode.noRights: There were not enough rights to create the tunnel, so TUN is off. Install the background service in the advanced settings or run the application as administrator
tunMode.rightsDeclined: The rights prompt was declined, so the background service cannot be installed and TUN stays off
tunMode.serviceSilent: The background service is installed but does not answer, so TUN does not work yet. Try repairing it in the advanced settings
tunMode.setupPending: The system rights prompt is still open — confirm it. TUN will turn on as soon as the service is installed
tunMode.setupBusy: The service setup is already running — wait for it to finish and try again
tunMode.adapterBusy: The TUN adapter is held by another client or was not released: close it or restart the computer
tunMode.setupStarted: Setting up TUN mode: installing the background service
tunMode.setupFailed: Could not install the background service, so TUN stays off
tunMode.noTraffic: TUN is up but no traffic is flowing through the tunnel
tunMode.noTrafficWindows: TUN is up but no traffic is flowing: allow the core through the Windows firewall for inbound connections or change the stack. Active stack

core.binaryChanged: The core file changed since it was installed and was not started
core.crashed: The core keeps crashing and was not restarted
core.handoffFailed: Handing the core over to the background service failed and it could not be brought back — the core is not running
core.notReady: The core started but does not answer, so the launch was cancelled
core.portBusy: Port {{port}} is held by another application: the core is not listening on it, so traffic will not go through the system proxy.
core.portBusyAction: Change the port in the settings
core.restarted: The core crashed and was restarted

service.bundleRejected: This configuration cannot be handed to the background service — the core runs without it and TUN is unavailable. Fix the configuration, then restart the core or switch TUN off and on again
service.needsRepair: The background service is outdated after the update. Repair it in the settings — TUN may not work until then

tooltips.systemProxy: Enable to modify the operating system's proxy settings. If enabling fails, modify the operating system's proxy settings manually
tooltips.tunMode: Tun (Virtual NIC) mode: Captures all system traffic, when enabled, there is no need to enable system proxy.
tooltips.tunUnavailable: TUN requires Service Mode or Admin Mode
tooltips.serviceOutdated: The TUN service is left over from an older app version and needs repair

messages.incomplete: Please fill in all required tunnel fields

tooltips.ipv6: IPv6 is set by the subscription: the value comes from its template, so this switch has no effect. When the subscription says nothing about IPv6, it stays off.
tooltips.unifiedDelay: Unified delay runs two measurements instead of one so that nodes of different types compare fairly. “As in the subscription” takes the value from the subscription template; a value chosen here wins over the subscription.
tooltips.logLevel: Core log level (the core file in the logs folder). “As in the subscription” takes the level from the subscription template; a level chosen here wins over the subscription and survives its updates.
tooltips.openUwpTool: Since Windows 8, UWP apps (such as Microsoft Store) are restricted from directly accessing local host network services, and this tool can be used to bypass this restriction
tooltips.routingMode: Rule routing sends only what the rules match through the proxy; global routes everything, direct nothing.
tooltips.dnsOverwrite: Careful: while this is on, the DNS block from the subscription is fully replaced by these settings.

advancedGroup.title: Advanced settings
advancedGroup.hint: Core, network, diagnostics and technical screens

basicGroup.hint: Language, theme, app appearance and notifications

hints.subNotifications: Warn about the subscription running out of traffic or time. Off silences these alerts regardless of the provider settings.
hints.deviceIdentity: Sends a hashed device id (x-hwid) with every subscription request so the provider can enforce its device limit. The raw machine id never leaves the device. Turning it off may make the panel refuse the subscription.
hints.windowFitContent: The window sizes its height to what is on the screen, so nothing hides behind a scrollbar. Resizing the window by hand turns this off and keeps your size.

tooltips.backupInfo: Support local or WebDAV backup of configuration files
tooltips.openConfDir: If the software runs abnormally, BACKUP and delete all files in this folder then restart the software
tooltips.liteMode: Close the GUI and keep only the kernel running
tooltips.supportBundle: Copies versions, core and subscription state and the tail of both logs — with subscription addresses, tokens and secrets already masked. Paste it into the provider's support chat.
tooltips.receivePrereleases: Update to alpha and beta versions as well. With this switched off only stable releases arrive.

fields.providerThemeHint: Accent, theme and background from the subscription — until you set your own

tooltips.hoverNavigator: Automatically scroll to the corresponding proxy group when hovering over alphabet letters
